newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA UNCHANGED FOR FIRST TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SOUTH AFRICA UNCHANGED FOR FIRST TEST.

text.p: South Africa have named an unchanged side for the first rugby union test against France in Bordeaux next Saturday.

A team spokesman said on Sunday that coach Andre Markgraaff picked the same side that beat Argentina 44-21 in the second test in Buenos Aires last weekend following the Springboks' 30-22 defeat by the French Barbarians on Saturday.
He said the reserves for the first test would probably also be the same but that Markgraaff had delayed a decision until after the match against a regional selection in Lyon on Tuesday.
But he said the Springboks had suffered no injuries in Brive on Saturday in their first defeat in the fifth match of a 10-match three-country tour of Argentina, France and Wales.
"It was a quite wonderful experience not to have any injuries. There was a Frenchman hurt, but none of ours," he said.
France, who also named their first test side on Saturday, were forced by injuries to key players to make five changes from the 40-33 victory over Wales in September.
In the absence of wing Philippe Saint-Andre they will be captained by flanker Abdelatif Benazzi.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert; 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier; 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron.

France - 15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Richard Dourthe, 13-Stephane Glas, 12-Thomas Castaignede, 11-David Berty; 10-Alain Penaud, 9-Philippe Carbonneau; 8-Thierry Labrousse, 7-Abdelatif Benazzi (captain), 6-Philippe Benetton, 5-Fabien Pelous, 4-Hugues Miorin, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc de Rougemont, 1-Christian Califano.
